summary.intent: Make parseBody and the json/form validators match Content-Type media types case-insensitively, keeping parameter values such as the multipart boundary intact.
summary.issue_fit: Partial. The three suggested cases from #5060 are implemented and tested, but the parseFormData rewrite breaks parseBody for a request whose formData() was already read.
summary.coverage: Complete: all six changed files reviewed; focused vitest runs at head pass (106 passed, 1 skipped; then 88 passed). One must-fix regression, confirmed by a fresh-context verifier. The verifier's proposed validator-first trigger was refuted by a probe, so it is not part of the finding.
check_details: Reviewer ran `./node_modules/.bin/vitest --run --project main --coverage.enabled=false` on body.test.ts, buffer.test.ts, validator.test.ts at the reviewed head: 106 passed, 1 skipped, exit 0.
Reviewer ran the same command on request.test.ts, middleware/method-override, and body.test.ts at the reviewed head: 88 passed, exit 0.
Reviewer scratch probe (esbuild bundle of head, main, and head with parseFormData reverted) confirmed the regression and the revert; not a repository check.

findings.title: Stop parseBody breaking after formData() has been read
findings.trigger: A handler calls c.req.formData() and then c.req.parseBody() on the same request.
findings.impact: On this head the second call throws `Failed to parse body as FormData` for multipart bodies, and returns one corrupt key holding re-serialized multipart text for urlencoded bodies; main returns the fields.
findings.change: In `parseFormData`, read the body with `(request as Request).formData()` again so HonoRequest's `bodyCache` is reused. The media-type guard in `parseBody` alone fixes the mixed-case issue, since the platform parser already accepts mixed-case media types.
findings.source: Issue #5060, expected behavior: supported media types match case-insensitively, and existing parsing is otherwise preserved.

observations.fact: The platform Request and Response formData() already accept mixed-case media types, so the buffer.ts lowercasing and the parseFormData rewrite are not needed for the fix.
observations.evidence: Probe: `new Request(..., {'Content-Type': 'Multipart/Form-Data; boundary=…'}).formData()` yields the field; `new Response(…, 'Application/X-WWW-Form-Urlencoded').formData()` yields `1`; `src/utils/buffer.ts:113`, `src/utils/body.ts:125-132`.

observations.fact: The method-override middleware still matches multipart and urlencoded Content-Type case-sensitively; this change does not touch it.
observations.evidence: `src/middleware/method-override/index.ts:74` and `:92` use `startsWith` on the raw header.

requirements.evidence: Matching is case-insensitive for the media-type portion and the boundary is preserved (body.test.ts, validator.test.ts, buffer.test.ts pass). The parseFormData rewrite regresses parseBody after formData(): see the finding.
parseBody x-www-form-urlencoded, validator('json') Application/JSON, validator('form') mixed-case urlencoded and multipart tests added and passing at head.
